body:
**Board organization above boards** · decided 2026-08-25, shipped 2026-08-26

**The answer: G + F, then E.**

- **G — Groups of boards** (rightmost frame) · explicit, coloured groups for areas of work — "Side pane", "Account page", "Navigation", "Brand" — each holding boards; boards keep their frames and screens exactly as today. `config.boardGroups` + `group?` on the board. MCP surface is one optional `group` arg on `add_board`/`update_board` (naming a new one creates it); all group management lives in the canvas. **Shipped.**
- **F — Multiple design folders per repo** (row 2) · the project layer, where the whole field puts it. `velloo init` offers to create another; `velloo folder list|add|remove` manages them; `velloo run` starts them all. **Shipped.**
- **E — Canvas regions** · the same idea one level down, and the primitive is already in the schema. **Still open.**

**Not doing:** A as drawn (superseded by G, which is A's model with E's colour language) · **B** (retired — projects are answered by F) · **C**'s tags (pins + recency still worth taking on their own) · **D** (rejected: deriving groups from the name makes renaming silently refile a board).

**Competitor audit** (Figma · Penpot · Sketch · Framer · tldraw · Storybook · Miro · Paper · Onlook). Nobody nests filing inside a document; nesting lives above it, which is F. The one pure filing hierarchy in the field — Miro's Space sections, public beta 2026-08 — is one level, drag-to-file, coloured, over a flat pool: G. The write-up was session-scoped; the finding was recorded with the other focused audits.

Each frame's note carries the schema shape, MCP surface, migration and failure mode.

**A — Groups over the flat list**

A grouping layer *on top of* `boardOrder`. Boards remain a flat pool of files; a group is a label + an ordered id list. Collapsible headers, a drop target per group, an implicit "Ungrouped" bucket for everything an agent just created, Archived stays where it is.

- **Schema** — `config.boardGroups: [{ id, name, boards: string[], collapsed?: boolean }]` next to `boardOrder`. No new files, no board-file change, no id rewrite. Absent field = today's behaviour, so every existing folder is already valid: zero migration.
- **MCP** — additive: optional `group` on `add_board`, a `group` field in `list_boards` output, `set_board_group` (or fold it into `update_board`). An agent that ignores all of it still works — its board lands in Ungrouped, visible, not lost.
- **UX** — group header = create / rename / collapse / delete-group-keep-boards. Drag a board between groups; dragging within a group reorders. Top bar shows `Group / Board` so the canvas says where you are.
- **Failure mode** — grouping is advisory. Nothing stops two groups from being conceptually the same, and a board can only sit in one. If the folder is 40 boards across 4 real workstreams, groups get long and the sidebar still scrolls.
- **Cost** — smallest of the three. Schema field + one mutation + sidebar drag/collapse work.

**B — Projects (first-class, two levels)**

A project owns its boards. The sidebar scopes to one project at a time — the switcher replaces the list, so a 40-board folder shows six rows. Figma's file/page split, and the shape `velloo.json` already uses one level up (named projects per repo).

- **Schema** — a real entity: `boards/<project>/<board>.json`, or `projects: [{ id, name, boards: [...] }]` in config with flat files. Either way board ids need a scope (two projects will both want `landing`), which means **migration** for every existing multi-board folder + a default "Main" project everything lands in.
- **MCP** — not additive. `list_boards` becomes project-scoped or grows a `project` arg; `add_board` needs a project (or a default); `add_frame`/`get_board` need to resolve ids across scopes. Every agent prompt that says "list the boards" now has a hidden current-project. That's the real cost: **a wrong-project board is invisible**, not just badly filed.
- **UX** — best at scale, worst at small scale: a 3-board folder pays a switcher and one extra click for nothing. Cross-project work (a shared brand board) has no answer without duplication or links.
- **Failure mode** — hidden state. Agents don't have a selected project the way a human does, so they need it passed explicitly every call or they'll all pile into the default.
- **Cost** — highest. Schema break, migration, MCP surface change, id-scoping rules.

**C — Flat + facets (no hierarchy)**

Keep one list; make it navigable instead of nested. A filter box, tag chips with counts, a pinned section, and recency sections. Nothing to file, nothing to maintain, nothing to be in the wrong place — a board is found, not located.

- **Schema** — `boards/<id>.json` grows `tags?: string[]` and `pinned?: boolean`; `updatedAt` already exists via mtime. `boardOrder` untouched. Fully additive, zero migration, and a board with no tags is exactly as usable as today.
- **MCP** — optional `tags` on `add_board`/`update_board`, `tags` in `list_boards`, an optional `tag` filter. Agents can tag on creation from context ("this is a brand board") without ever needing to know a container exists — the one model that fits how agents actually work.
- **UX** — one board can carry several tags (`explorations` + `canvas`), which A and B both forbid. Pins keep the two boards you're actually in at the top. Reuses ⌘K search, already shipped.
- **Failure mode** — no structure means no *shared* structure: tags drift (`brand`, `branding`), and with 40 untagged boards it degrades back to today's scroll. It organizes retrieval, not the mental model — there's no "these five boards are one piece of work" object to hand to a teammate or publish.
- **Cost** — low. Two optional fields, a filter + chips in the sidebar, no new mutation semantics.

**Not exclusive** — C is the cheap floor under either. A + C (groups *and* tags/pins) is the combination worth costing before choosing; B only earns its migration if folders are heading past ~30 boards or projects become a publish/share boundary.

**D — Derived groups — REJECTED 2026-08-25**

The idea: group by the name prefix, Storybook-style — `Canvas — Settings dialog` collapses under a `Canvas` header, computed, never stored. It cost nothing and would have grouped 22 of the 39 boards across the local folders on day one.

**Why it's out:** it's magical, and it breaks renaming. A rename is the most ordinary edit there is, and under D it silently refiles the board — drop the prefix and the board leaves its group; typo the prefix and it forms a group of one. The mechanism is invisible at the moment you need it to be obvious, and there's no way to say "keep this name, change the grouping" or the reverse. Cheap to build, expensive to live in.

Superseded by **G**: an explicit group, coloured, edited in the canvas — where renaming a board and refiling it stay two different actions.

Kept on the board as a recorded rejection.

**E — Groups as canvas regions (the primitive that already exists)**

The field's near-universal second answer: Figma sections, Miro and tldraw frames, Penpot nested boards, Paper artboards. `BoardGroup` is already in the schema — `{ id, name, color? }` on the board, frames carry the group id — with `addGroup`/`updateGroup`/`removeGroup` written in `mutations/groups.ts`. Missing: HTTP exposure and any canvas UI.

- **Region geometry is derived**, not stored. The tint is the bounding box of the member frames, so moving a frame re-fits the region and nothing can go stale. That's why the schema only holds name + colour.
- **The sidebar gets a second level for free.** Expand the active board and its groups are listed with their colour chips and counts; clicking one zooms the canvas to that region. This is hierarchy that *means* something — it maps to what you can see — which is the audit's test for hierarchy that lasts (Framer's page tree = URL structure, Storybook's = component paths).
- **It doesn't fix the sidebar list.** Our folders inflate by workstream (`Team`, `Cloud`, `Brand`), not by variant — those are already multi-frame boards. E is why a variant set should never *become* three boards; D is what to do about the workstreams that legitimately are separate boards. Different problems, both worth solving.
- **Cost** — the mutations exist. Needed: HTTP routes, `group` on the frame inspector, drag-into-region, ⌘G on a selection, region rendering + hit-testing under zoom, and the sidebar disclosure. Bigger than D, smaller than B.

**F — Multiple design folders per repo (the Figma "folder" layer)**

Decision taken 2026-08-25: a repo can hold several design folders, and `velloo init` on a repo that already has one should offer to create another. This is the layer the audit found everyone puts nesting on — Figma renamed Projects → Folders with 10-level nesting (2026-08-03), Miro renamed Projects → Spaces, Penpot and Sketch both keep projects above the file.

**Most of it already exists.** `velloo.json` (shipped 2026-07-10, decision recorded in m-24) names design folders as projects; all ten CLI commands resolve a project name or a path; `velloo status` labels running daemons by project name; `init` already calls `registerProject`. What's missing is only the two things in these frames.

**F1 — the init prompt.** Today `velloo init` on an existing design offers Connect agents / Re-scaffold (overwrite) / Cancel (`commands/init.ts:582`). Add "Create another design folder" as the first option, then ask for a path (rejecting an existing design folder) and a `velloo.json` project name, and fall through to the normal wizard. Agent wiring is per-folder, so the second folder registers its own MCP server with the same client. Small, contained change.

**F2 — the canvas needs to admit the other folders exist.** A folder chip in the top bar reads `velloo.json` and lists the repo's folders with their daemon state; a running one opens its port, a stopped one offers Start, and "New design folder…" points at `velloo init`. Switching **navigates to that folder's own canvas** — it does not merge them. That respects the per-folder daemon decision and the 2026-07-10 rejection of a single canvas service per machine: this is within one repo, reading a file that's already there, and every folder keeps its own daemon, MCP endpoint, history and theme.

**How this changes the hierarchy question.** With F shipped, "projects" is answered at the folder layer, exactly as the field answers it — which is what retires option B and leaves the in-folder question (D + E) as the only one left to decide.

**G — Groups of boards (the pick, 2026-08-25)**

A's data model with E's visual language. A group is an *area of work* — "Side pane", "Account page", "Navigation", "Brand" — holding a set of boards; each board stays exactly what it is today, with its own frames and screens.

- **Schema** — `config.boardGroups: [{ id, name, color? }]` plus `group?: string` on the board file (mirroring how a frame carries its `BoardGroup` id — same shape, one level up). `boardOrder` keeps ordering *within* a group; a board with no `group` falls into the implicit Ungrouped section. Absent field = today's sidebar, so no migration.
- **MCP** — no group CRUD tools. `add_board` and `update_board` take an optional `group`; naming a group that doesn't exist creates it (colour auto-assigned from the palette). `list_boards` returns each board's group. That's the whole agent surface — an agent can file a board it just made, and can't otherwise reorganise the folder.
- **Canvas owns grouping.** Create / rename / recolour / reorder / collapse and delete-group-keep-boards all live in the sidebar. Board ⋯ → "Move to group ▸" with the colour chips, drag a row into a group, drop-target highlight on the group header. The group is a coloured chip in the top-bar crumb, matching E's region colours.
- **Why not D** — deriving groups from a name prefix looked free but makes renaming load-bearing and surprising: rename a board and it silently refiles itself. Rejected 2026-08-25.
- **Why not B** — projects are answered one level up, by multiple design folders in `velloo.json` (frames F1/F2).
- **Pairs with E**, which is the same idea inside a board: regions group frames, groups group boards, both coloured, both derived-geometry-free. Ship G first (it's the list that hurts), E after.
